gloss: unable to read the room, socially clueless

definitions.gloss: unable to read the room, socially oblivious
definitions.explanation: Describes a person who fails to pick up on the unspoken atmosphere or social cues in a situation. Often abbreviated to KY (ケーワイ).

examples.japanese: ⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧、{空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: That person can't read the room, can they?

examples.japanese: ⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧にしてる⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦なんて→なんて：06918_nante⟧、{空気|くうき}{読|よ}めないな。
examples.english: Talking loudly when everyone else is being quiet — that's really not reading the room.

examples.japanese: {空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}われたくない→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I don't want to be seen as someone who can't read the room, so I try to pay attention to my surroundings.

notes:
{空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない literally means "cannot read the air." In Japanese culture, ⟦{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む→空気を読む：06306_kuukiwoyomu⟧ (reading the air/atmosphere) is a key social skill — sensing unspoken moods, expectations, and group dynamics.

FORMS:
KY (ケーワイ) is a widely known abbreviation for ⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧. It became popular slang in the mid-2000s and is still understood, though somewhat dated.
- ⟦{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む→空気を読む：06306_kuukiwoyomu⟧: to read the room (positive)
- ⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧: cannot read the room
- {空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a socially clueless person
- KY: abbreviation (used as a label)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese communication relies heavily on implicit understanding. Being able to "read the air" — understanding what is not said — is considered a fundamental social skill. People who miss these cues may be criticized as ⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧. This reflects the broader Japanese value of ⟦{察|さっ}する→察する：08053_sassuru⟧ (perceiving unstated feelings).

The concept is so central that its opposite, ⟦{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む→空気を読む：06306_kuukiwoyomu⟧, is taught as a life skill, and KY became a cultural buzzword describing people who disrupt social harmony.
